subject: Logic
title: Omelas
description: A micro-lesson that makes Omelas usable.

hook.text: A perfect city of joy and abundance—but its happiness depends on the suffering of one child locked in a basement.

buildup.text: Ursula K. Le Guin's story asks: is it moral to accept a paradise built on the misery of one innocent person?

discovery.text: Most citizens accept the trade. Utilitarianism supports it—maximum happiness for maximum people.

twist.text: But some people walk away from Omelas. They reject a society that requires any innocent to suffer for others' joy.

climax.text: The experiment doesn't give an answer. It asks what you'd do—and what that reveals about your moral framework.

punchline.text: Would you stay? Would you walk away?

quiz.question: What moral question does Omelas pose?
options: Whether a society's happiness can justify one person's suffering
